kayamkulam_frontier.label: Kayamkulam frontier ridges
kayamkulam_frontier.anchor: Rolling ridges of red earth and gold grass on the Kayamkulam frontier, thin threads of smoke rising from small village fires. On the nearest ridge the raw new laterite wall of a Travancore fort rises behind bamboo scaffolding with small masons on it, and below it a local chief's tiled house stands among pepper gardens, its people in the yard looking up.
kayamkulam_frontier.absent: No coast, sea or ships; no European bastions or finished stone castle; no identifiable principal in the landscape.

frontier_fort.label: Courtyard and verandah of the new frontier fort
frontier_fort.anchor: The courtyard of the new Travancore frontier fort: fresh red laterite walls still raw at the edges, packed red earth underfoot, and a shaded verandah under a sloping tiled roof on timber posts along one side. Drink is served in clay cups; anyone seated sits on a mat or the verandah edge.
frontier_fort.absent: No chairs, benches, European bastions, blue coats or red coats. Where the old grey-bearded trader appears he is not Yusuf: bare-headed and bare-chested, with no skullcap, coat or scar.
frontier_fort.time: dry morning light and deep verandah shade

column_track.label: Red dirt track on the frontier march
column_track.anchor: A red dirt track through dry frontier scrub and pepper country with the mixed column strung along it: light Maravar horse, Madurai lancers, a core of Maratha riders around Nagoji, Nair musketeers in white on foot with long Indian matchlocks shouldered, and a light gun on a two-wheeled carriage drawn by bullocks.
column_track.absent: No European uniforms, red or blue coats, bayonets or flintlocks, and no flag with writing or emblem. The Maratha riders wear white or cream pagdis, never a rust-red turban with a red sash.

village_festival.label: Village temple festival on the frontier
village_festival.anchor: A modest village shrine between Padmini's lands and the hills: a Kerala gatehouse with a low sloping tiled roof and carved wooden figures on its gables, oil lamps in niches along the laterite outer wall, and bright cloths tied between the trees. Drummers and nadaswaram players, a flower-decked palanquin with a simple wooden goddess, a tusker with a gold nettipattam and food stalls ring a barefoot crowd carrying small clay lamps.
village_festival.absent: No tall stone gopuram tower, glass lanterns, chairs or European figures. No one but Ponnan wears red cloth.
village_festival.time: dusk, open-wick clay lamps lighting faces from below

convoy_road.label: Raided convoy on the frontier road
convoy_road.anchor: A dry roadside in the frontier hills: an overturned grain cart, spilled paddy across red dirt, and three still shapes under cloths along the verge. A torn strip of blue-and-white checked cloth and a few plain silver coins are the only foreign trace.
convoy_road.absent: No blood, wounds or faces of the dead; no Dutch soldiers, coats or flags; no lettering, monogram or mark on the cloth or the coins.

kollamkara_valley.label: Valley road held by the Kollamkara Raja
kollamkara_valley.anchor: A narrow valley where the road dips between two wooded slopes of red earth and dry scrub: a line of spearmen and archers across the road, men with long Indian matchlocks and smouldering slow-match on both slopes, and banners of bright plain cloth on tall poles in a hot wind. The raja's low wooden stool stands in the exact centre of the road.
kollamkara_valley.absent: No Dutch soldiers, blue coats, European muskets or bayonets; no writing or emblem on the banners; no fort or walls in the valley. The raja's men wear no red, which is Ponnan's alone.
kollamkara_valley.time: hot late morning, hard light and dry wind

burned_gardens.label: Padmini's burned pepper gardens
burned_gardens.anchor: A strip of Padmini's pepper gardens along a canal, vines torched, support poles cut and red soil trampled under thick black smoke. From the ridge the raiders in plain cloth withdraw small into the scrub; close in, two of her men lie still beside the path.
burned_gardens.absent: No blood or wounds; no company colours, Dutch muskets or blue coats among the raiders; no fort and no European figures.
burned_gardens.time: daylight dimmed by smoke, two weeks after the standoff

scrub_chase.label: Chase track and ambush bend in the scrub
scrub_chase.anchor: A narrow track between red rock outcrops, branches whipping across it and a shallow stream running over mossy stones, closing into a tight bend with a side thicket. Travancore riders in white on light horses; the ambushers are bare-chested men in plain cloth with long Indian matchlocks and bows.
scrub_chase.absent: No blood or drawn wounds; no Dutch muskets, bayonets, coats or banners. Red cloth is Ponnan's alone.
scrub_chase.time: broken daylight under branches, white powder smoke at the bend

thorn_ridge.label: Ridge above the thorn valley
thorn_ridge.anchor: A rocky ridge crest above a shallow valley choked with low thorn bushes and outcrops, where the riders rein in and the light gun on its two-wheeled bullock carriage is hauled to the edge. The valley floor lies far below between the thorn stands.
thorn_ridge.absent: No wall, fort or village as the gun's target; no European gunners, uniforms or coats; no blood, and any stains read dark, never red.

thorn_valley.label: Inside the thorn valley
thorn_valley.anchor: Inside the thorn: close, dim and green-brown, thorns catching at cloth among rocky outcrops and loose stones, banks of white powder smoke drifting through, and a pale rock face where the scrub ends. The raiders are bare-chested or in torn plain cloth, with spears, swords, daggers and long matchlocks.
thorn_valley.absent: No blood, red blades or drawn wounds: the fallen lie still and whole, and blades and stains read dark, never red. Red cloth is Ponnan's alone.
thorn_valley.time: late afternoon light filtered through thorn and powder smoke

audience_hall.label: Pillared audience hall of the fort
audience_hall.anchor: A closed-door council in the fort's pillared audience hall: laterite walls, timber pillars, a carved teak ceiling, a grey stone floor and a tall doorway at the far end. Ramayyan sits cross-legged at a low writing desk with an open palm-leaf bundle, its cord loosened, and an iron stylus.
audience_hall.absent: No black polished floor or ship-prow roof, which belong to the palace room; no throne, chairs, benches, paper scroll or court audience.
audience_hall.time: cool daylight from the tall doorway

nagoji_quarters.label: Nagoji's quarters
nagoji_quarters.anchor: A plain room in Nagoji's quarters: laterite walls, a timber doorway, a woven mat on the floor, a brass basin on a low stand and a single clay open-wick lamp between the figures.
nagoji_quarters.absent: No glass lantern, chairs, European bed or mirror; the basin water is at most faintly pink and clearing, never red.
nagoji_quarters.time: the hour before dawn, one clay lamp and the doorway still dark

padmanabhaswamy_temple.label: Padmanabhaswamy temple
padmanabhaswamy_temple.anchor: The great Padmanabhaswamy temple under a hard sky: the tall tiered stone gopuram, a ring of belikal offering stones, and temple elephants darker than night, draped in silks, swaying in the gopuram's shade. A barefoot crowd presses toward the royal party behind a line of white-clad escort spearmen.
padmanabhaswamy_temple.absent: No boots, glass lamps or European figures; no crest, crown, turban or spear on Varma; no blood, drawn wound or body of the attacker.
padmanabhaswamy_temple.time: hard bright midday under a pale sky

palace_room.label: Palace room with the black polished floor
palace_room.anchor: A palace room with a black polished floor and a ship-prow timber roof of carved beams, timber pillars and a doorway, lit only by clay and brass open-wick oil lamps whose shadows climb the carved ceiling. Varma rests on a low wooden couch; physicians, when present, tend the back of his LEFT shoulder.
palace_room.absent: No European bed, chairs or glass lamps; no throne, crown or turban; no grey stone floor. No blood: the wound stays under pastes and cloth, and any dark patch is kept in shadow.
palace_room.time: oil lamplight only, deep shadow beyond the flames

palace_corridor.label: Lamplit palace corridor
palace_corridor.anchor: The long corridor outside the king's room: the black polished floor gleaming under a row of clay and brass open-wick lamps, timber pillars and carved beams receding in deep perspective.
palace_corridor.absent: No glass lamps, European furniture or extra figures; Varma stays in the room behind them.

character_notes.nagoji: Thick curled moustache; clean-shaven chin and jaw, smooth skin, no beard or facial scar; a tiny flush gold ear stud on the lobe with nothing hanging from it. Kerala topknot with first grey at the temples, no turban and no red sash; the old brand and long white scar sit on the inner LEFT forearm a hand's width above the wrist, and the healed LEFT palm shows only a faint pale line, no bandage.
character_notes.ponnan: Broad-shouldered Maravar with curly hair and NO topknot, thick moustache and clean chin; red shoulder cloth, short jacket, white mundu hitched to bare knees. The red shoulder cloth is his alone in this chapter, and his smaller Maravar horse stands a head lower than Kayal.
character_notes.kayal: Bay mare with an ochre red-brown coat, black mane, tail and lower legs and no white markings, sized between a heavy charger and a small Maravar pony.
character_notes.padmini: In her fifties, thick black hair threaded with grey and coiled at the nape, simple gold and a long walking stick, never a cane; cream sari with a narrow gold border hitched for riding, old Kerala drape with no stitched blouse. Only the remembered younger Padmini of the canal-bank inset has black hair with no grey.
character_notes.varma: Face, moustache and build from his sheet with black hair, bare-headed with his hair in a side knot above the LEFT ear: no turban, crest or crown anywhere in this chapter, whatever the sheet shows. At the temple he is bare-chested in a white mundu and white silk angavastram with heavy rings, sandal paste on the brow and no spear; the knife wound and later the bandage sit at the back of his LEFT shoulder only from the attack onward, never the right and never before it.
character_notes.ramayyan: Thin sharp fine features and receding hair, plain unbordered white cloth, no forehead marks or sacred thread; palm-leaf bundle and iron stylus, never a paper scroll. Never the temple priest's face.
character_notes.kollamkara: Heavy and sharp-eyed, flesh hanging a little over the sash; bare-chested in a white mundu with a broad gold-edged waist sash, no leather belt, heavy gold ear hoops and neck chains and a worn-hilted sword at the sash. No coat or jacket; in the canal-bank inset he is the same man years younger and thinner.
character_notes.prince: A boy of about ten with his uncle's sharp cheekbones and wide watchful eyes, bare-chested in a small white silk mundu with a thin gold chain.
character_notes.yusuf: Tall and lean, white skullcap, neatly trimmed dark beard, short coat over a white tunic, no vest, no turban and no facial scar, so he never reads as his scarred cousin.
